items.title: Nepal travel agents threaten to stop selling Thailand trips over visa rules
items.desc: NATTA says travellers risk losing money on flights and hotel bookings paid for before visa approval, and warns it may redirect customers to other destinations if the problems persist.

items.title: Karan KC’s late heroics take Nepal to 263/8 against Oman
items.desc: KC smashed a quickfire 40 off 16 before getting run out in the last ball of the first innings.

items.title: Police await complaint to investigate audio clip linked to RSP lawmaker
items.desc: The Rastriya Swatantra Party has launched an internal inquiry into allegations against Khagendra Sunar, while police say they need a formal complaint to begin a criminal investigation.

items.title: Bailey bridge planned at flood-damaged Arughat crossing
items.desc: A 22-metre section of the bridge was washed away by the Budhi Gandaki flood on Sunday, halting traffic between Gorkha and Dhading. Authorities aim to complete the temporary crossing within 10 days.

items.title: Indian police detain ‘cockroach’ movement leaders demanding election chief’s resignation
items.desc: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party and opposition groups accuse the Election Commission of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP, a charge the poll panel denies.

items.title: Lawmaker Khagendra Sunar denies blackmail allegations, blames AI smear campaign
items.desc: Sunar says allegations against him are fabricated and has pledged to cooperate with investigations by his party and the government.

items.title: 14 internet providers fined for overcharging customers
items.desc: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority has fined the companies Rs50,000 each, ordered the withdrawal of unauthorised packages and directed compensation for customers who suffered losses.

items.title: Swarnim Wagle heads to Bangkok for World Bank, IMF meetings
items.desc: The finance minister is scheduled to hold more than 16 bilateral and multilateral meetings on Nepal’s economic priorities and development financing.

items.title: How Nepal’s provinces have become ‘factories’ for ministers
items.desc: Since 2023, more than half of Nepal’s provincial lawmakers have held ministerial office. This political volatility has left hospitals short of medicine and half-built projects on the brink of decay.

items.title: RSP orders probe into allegations against lawmaker Khagendra Sunar
items.desc: Sunar has been told to stay away from formal public events in his official capacity until the party’s inquiry concludes.

items.title: Mental Wellbeing: What if ‘Thik cha’ isn’t the whole story?
items.desc: In a society where we often say we are fine even when we are struggling, making space for honest conversations can be a meaningful first step towards better mental health.

items.title: Budhigandaki flood victims struggle to find shelter
items.desc: More than 200 homes were swept away in Gorkha, while destroyed bridges and trails have left northern settlements cut off from relief supplies.

items.title: Their flood videos went viral. They are still haunted by what they saw
items.desc: Millions watched videos of the August 26 flood that devastated entire towns. The men behind two of the clips survived, but one lost his home and farmland, the other his mother.

items.title: Envoy nominees face abuse, extortion and conflict-of-interest complaints
items.desc: The proposed envoys to Saudi Arabia and Japan face questions over alleged violence against a woman, financial wrongdoing, permanent residency and potential conflicts of interest.

items.title: Bhutanese refugee scam victims awarded Rs 153.8 million, but 53 complainants get no compensation
items.desc: The Kathmandu District Court’s full verdict, issued recently, details how a network duped aspiring migrants with promises of US resettlement.

items.title: Explained: Why does an hour long flight to Dhangadhi cost more than a flight to New Delhi?
items.desc: Domestic airfares in Nepal have doubled on the longest route in 12 years, with rising fuel costs, taxes and seasonal demand pushing up ticket prices.

items.title: Nepal begins CAR T-cell therapy for cancer patients
items.desc: A 20-year-old woman with relapsed leukaemia has received the treatment at TU Teaching Hospital. Doctors are monitoring her response.

items.title: Lawmakers press envoy nominees to India, China, US, and UK on challenges
items.desc: Candidates faced scrutiny over unresolved border disputes, cross-border connectivity, economic cooperation, and the welfare of Nepali citizens abroad.

items.title: Nepal’s provinces must stop manufacturing ministers and start governing
items.desc: With 55 percent of provincial lawmakers having served as ministers, the provinces need to put governing ahead of oath-taking.

items.title: Can Himalayan floods bridge the India-China divide?
items.desc: When a few hours’ notice can save lives, fragmented or missing cross-country information becomes dangerous.

items.title: Dismantle party-affiliated student unions without hindering student politics
items.desc: Political parties’ historical contributions do not give them a license to control universities and student bodies.

items.title: Nepal seek momentum against Oman
items.desc: Out of top-four contention for a direct World Cup Qualifier berth, the Rhinos target momentum in Oman before entering the Qualifier’s Playoff stage.

items.title: Parliamentary hearing committee invites complaints against four Supreme Court nominees
items.desc: The public has 10 days to file complaints against the four judges recommended for appointment to the Supreme Court.

items.title: India opposition parties march to Supreme Court against election chief
items.desc: The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol.

items.title: More than 32,500 armed police personnel mobilised for festival security
items.desc: The Armed Police Force has deployed 28,126 personnel and kept another 4,500 on standby for Dashain, Tihar, Chhath and other festivals.

items.title: Americans Hall, Woodford win Nobel prize for work on stabilising economies
items.desc: The prestigious award, formally known as the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in ​Memory of Alfred Nobel, is the final prize to be given out this year and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns.

items.title: Budhigandaki flood: What the report says about the gap between local warnings and official records
items.desc: A driver received a flood warning at 4:45am on Sunday and posted an alert on Facebook minutes later, while the disaster authority’s report says a landslide blocked the river at 5:30am.

items.title: Court ruling leads to cancellation of ‘Perfect Center Fillz’ trademark
items.desc: The Department of Industry cancelled the registration after the Supreme Court found the chewing gum brand’s name too similar to Italian confectionery maker Perfetti Van Melle’s ‘Center Fruit’ trademark.

items.title: Government withdraws five police personnel from UML headquarters
items.desc: The personnel were recalled from the party’s Chyasal office on Monday morning, prompting the UML to consider alternative security arrangements.
